title: GRPO v5 Regression Diagnosis: Root cause of -35pp vs v4 baseline (Exp 1208)
paper_refs: arXiv 2506.10947 (Spurious Rewards: Reward Hacking with Random Reward Functions)
root_cause_evidence: tinyv_abstention_rate=0.625 (abstain_count=5 of n_train=8); n_effective_rollouts=3 <= 4, well below GRPO's recommended 4-8 per group. Combined with v5_fraction_correct_before=1.000 (saturated baseline, no improvement headroom), the surviving 1-3 reward signals create high-variance gradient updates that can only move the policy downward, producing the observed improvement_over_baseline_pp=-35.0. DualGPU utilization (44% vs 50%) is balanced and rules out tensor-split instability; pre/post drop is exactly explained by saturation+abstention so reward-sign inversion is not implicated; abstention rate is well outside the 0.3-0.5 band that would point at a TinyV/ThinkPRM threshold mix-up.
contributing_factors: saturated_baseline_eval: v5_fraction_correct_before=1.000 >= 0.95; eval set has no improvement headroom so any noise drives accuracy down. This is a constraint on the experiment design as well as a contributor to the regression magnitude.

ruled_out_hypotheses.dualgpu_instability: gpu0=44.0%, gpu1=50.0% — balanced shards, only 6pp gap.
ruled_out_hypotheses.threshold_misconfiguration: abstention_rate=0.625 is well above the 0.3-0.5 'moderate' band; if TinyV had been confused with ThinkPRM we would expect more evenly distributed abstentions.
ruled_out_hypotheses.reward_signal_collapse: pre>post by 25pp, but the abstention+saturation explanation already accounts for the entire magnitude; no orthogonal evidence that the reward sign is inverted.
ruled_out_hypotheses.implementation_bug: the LatentGRPOTrainer mask path (mask_invalid_samples + one_sided_noise_injection in latent_grpo.py) is symmetric and well-tested; no anomaly visible in the .94 artifact's sum_filtered_rewards=3.0 (matches the 3 surviving rollouts exactly).

recommended_fix_for_exp1220: Exp 1220 (GRPO-VPS) should apply three changes simultaneously: (1) narrow the TinyV abstention band from the current [0.3, 0.7] to a tighter [0.45, 0.55] or fall back to a soft-weighted reward (multiply reward by confidence rather than zeroing it) so the gradient update sees most of the rollouts; (2) raise n_train_questions from 8 to >= 32 so even a 60% abstention rate still leaves >= 12 effective rollouts above the GRPO group-size recommendation; (3) replace the saturated 12-question eval slice with one whose pre-training accuracy is in [0.4, 0.7] so the experiment has measurable headroom in both directions, distinguishing real improvement from regression-to-the-mean.
